40:60: The Imams, may God have mercy on them, differed regarding this second prostration in Surat al-Hajj 22:Is it permissible to prostrate in it, or not? There are two opinions. We have already mentioned the hadith of Uqbah ibn Amir from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding the first: Surat Al-Hajj is superior in that it has two prostrations, so whoever does not prostrate in them should not recite them. And His statement: And strive in God’s cause with the striving due to Him means with your wealth, your tongues, and yourselves, as God the Almighty said: And fear God with the fear He should be feared. And His saying: He has chosen you meaning, O this nation, God has chosen you and selected you over all other nations, and He has favored you and honored you and singled you out with the most honorable Messenger and the most perfect law. And He has not placed upon you in the religion any difficulty meaning, He has not burdened you with what you cannot bear and He has not obligated you with something that is difficult for you except that God has made for you a way out and relief. So the prayer, which is the greatest pillar of Islam after the two testimonies, is obligatory in the city as four, and when traveling it is shortened to two, and in fear some imams pray it as one rak’ah, as mentioned in the hadith, and it is prayed by men and riders facing the qiblah or not facing it, and likewise in the voluntary prayer while traveling toward the qiblah or otherwise, and standing in it is dropped due to the excuse of illness, so the sick person prays it sitting, and if he is unable to do so, then on his side, and other concessions and leniencies in all the obligatory and necessary prayers, and for this reason the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: I was sent with the easy-going Hanafiyyah and he said to Muadh and Abu Musa when he sent them as commanders to Yemen: Give good tidings and do not repel, and make things easy and do not… “In difficulty,” and there are many hadiths on this. That is why Ibn Abbas said in his statement: And He has not placed upon you in religion any difficulty, meaning any hardship. And his saying: The religion of your father Abraham Ibn Jarir said: It is accusative on the basis of He has not placed upon you in religion any difficulty meaning any hardship, rather He has made it easy for you, the religion of your father Abraham. He said: It is possible that it is accusative on the basis of the basis of the assumption: adhere to the religion of your father Abraham. I said and this meaning in this verse is like his saying: “Say: Indeed, my Lord has guided me to a straight path, a right religion, the religion of Abraham, the upright” the verse, and his saying: He named you Muslims before and in this Imam Abdullah bin Mubarak said on the authority of Ibn Jurayj on the authority of Ata’ on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his saying: He named you Muslims before he said: God Almighty, and this is what Mujahid, Ata’, Ad-Dahhak, As-Suddi, Muqatil bin Hayyan, and Qatadah said. And Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: He named you Muslims before, meaning Abraham, and that is His saying: Our Lord, and make us Muslims [in submission] to You and from our descendants a Muslim nation [in submission] to You. Ibn Jarir said: This has no basis, because it is known that Abraham did not name this nation Muslims in the Qur’an, and God Almighty said: He named you Muslims before and in this, Mujahid said: God named you Muslims before in the previous books and in the remembrance, and in this, meaning the Qur’an, and others said the same. I said And this is correct, because the Almighty said: He has chosen you and has not placed upon you in religion any difficulty. Then He urged them and tempted them to what the Messenger, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, brought, which is the religion of their father Abraham, the friend of God. Then He mentioned His favor upon this nation by mentioning it and praising it in ancient times and in the books of the prophets, recited to the rabbis and monks, and He said: He named you Muslims before, meaning before this Qur’an. And in this. Al-Nasa’i narrated when interpreting this verse: Hisham bin Ammar informed us, Muhammad bin Shu’aib informed us, Mu’awiyah bin Salam informed us that his brother Zaid bin Salam informed him on the authority of Abu Salam that he informed him, he said: Al-Harith Al-Ash’ari informed me on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, who said: Whoever calls with the call of the Age of Ignorance will be from the depths of Hell. A man said: O Messenger of God, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, even if he fasts and prays? He said: Yes, even if he fasts and prays. So call with the call of God by which He named you Muslims, believers, servants of God. God,” and we have presented this hadith in its entirety when explaining His statement, O mankind, worship your Lord, who created you and those before you, that you may become righteous, from Surat Al-Baqarah. For this reason, He said, That the Messenger may be a witness over you and you may be witnesses over the people, meaning, We have made you thus a just, good, and virtuous nation, whose justice is witnessed by all nations, so that on the Day of Resurrection you may be witnesses over the people, because all nations will recognize on that Day their sovereignty and superiority over every other nation. For this reason, their testimony against them will be accepted on the Day of Resurrection that the Messengers conveyed the message of their Lord to them, and the Messenger will bear witness over this nation that he conveyed it to them. We have already discussed this when He said, And thus We have made you a just community that you may be witnesses over the people and the Messenger may be a witness over you, and we have mentioned the hadith of Noah and his nation in a way that makes it unnecessary to repeat it. And His statement, So establish prayer and give zakat, meaning, meet this great blessing by thanking Him for it, so fulfill God’s right over you in performing what He has made obligatory, obeying what He has made obligatory, and avoiding what He has forbidden. Among the most important of these is establishing prayer and giving zakat, which is doing good to God’s creation by what He has made obligatory for the poor upon the rich by giving a small portion of his wealth each year to the weak and needy, as was explained and detailed in the verse on zakat in Surat At-Tawbah. And His statement, And hold fast to God, meaning, seek support from God, seek His help, rely on Him, and be supported by Him. He is your Protector, meaning He who protects you, supports you, and grants you victory over your enemies. What an excellent Protector and what an excellent Helper, meaning what an excellent Guardian and Helper from enemies. Wahib ibn Al-Ward said, God the Most High says: Son of Adam, remember Me when you are angry, and I will remember you when I am angry, so I will not annihilate you among those whom I annihilate. And if you are wronged, then be patient and accept My support, for My support for you is better than your support for yourself. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim, and God knows best. The last interpretation of Surat Al-Hajj, praise and thanks be to God. The last interpretation of Surat Al-Hajj, praise and thanks be to God. This is from His grace and generosity, the Blessed and Exalted, that He urged His servants to supplicate to Him and guaranteed to answer them, as Sufyan al-Thawri used to say: O He whose servants are most beloved to Him are those who ask Him and ask Him often, and O He whose servants are most hated by Him are those who do not ask Him, and no one is like that except You, O Lord. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim and in this meaning the poet says: God gets angry if you stop asking Him, and when a human being is asked, he gets angry. Qatada said: Kaab al-Ahbar said: This nation has been given three things that were not given to any nation or prophet before it: Whenever God sent a prophet, He would say to him: You are a witness over your nation and I have made you witnesses over the people. It would be said to him: There is no difficulty upon you in religion. He said to this nation: And He has not placed upon you in religion any difficulty. It would be said to him: Call upon Me and I will respond to you. He said to this nation: Call upon Me and I will respond to you. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Imam Al-Hafiz Abu Ya`la Ahmad bin Ali bin Al-Muthanna Al-Mawsili said in his Musnad: Abu Ibrahim Al-Tarjamani told us, Salih Al-Mari told us: I heard Al-Hasan narrating on the authority of Anas bin Malik, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in what he narrated on the authority of his Lord, the Almighty and Majestic, who said: “Four qualities, one of them is for Me, one is for you, one is between Me and you, and one is between you and My servants. As for the one that is for Me, then worship Me and do not associate anything with Me. As for the one that is for you, I will reward you for whatever good you do. As for the one that is between Me and you, then from you is the supplication and I will answer. As for the one that is between you and My servants, then be pleased with them as you would be pleased with yourself.” Imam Ahmad said: Abu Muawiyah told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Dhar, on the authority of Yasee’ Al-Kindi, on the authority of An-Nu’man ibn Bashir may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: Supplication is worship. Then he recited: “Call upon Me; I will respond to you. Indeed, those who disdain My worship will enter Hell in humiliation.” This is how the authors of the Sunans, At-Tirmidhi, An-Nasa’i, Ibn Majah, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Jarir, all narrated it on the authority of Al-A’mash. At-Tirmidhi said: It is hasan saheeh. Abu Dawud, At-Tirmidhi, An-Nasa’i, and Ibn Jarir also narrated it on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Al-Mansur and Al-A’mash, both of them on the authority of Dhar, on this authority. Ibn Yunus also narrated it on the authority of Asid ibn Asim ibn Mihran. An-Nu’man ibn Abd Al-Salam told us, Sufyan Ath-Thawri told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Dhar, on this authority. Ibn Hibban and Al-Hakim narrated it in their Saheehs, and Al-Hakim said: Its chain of transmission is saheeh. Imam Ahmad said: Waki’ Abu Malih Al-Madani, a sheikh from the people of Madinah, told us that he heard it from Abu Salih. He said once, “I heard Abu Salih narrating from Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Whoever does not supplicate to God Almighty, He becomes angry with him.’” Ahmad is the only one to narrate it, and this is a sound chain of transmission. Imam Ahmad also said: Marwan Al-Fazari told us, Subaih Abu Al-Malih told us, I heard Abu Salih narrating from Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Whoever does not ask of Him, He becomes angry with him.’ Ibn Ma’in said: This Abu Al-Malih’s name is Subaih, thus recorded it with the dammah by Abd Al-Ghani bin Sa’id. As for this Abu Salih, he is Al-Khawzi, who lived in Sha’b Al-Khawz. Al-Bazzar said this in his Musnad. This is how it appears in his narration: Abu Al-Malih Al-Farsi, from Abu Salih Al-Khawzi, from Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Whoever does not ask of God, He becomes angry with him.’” Abu Muhammad Al-Hasan bin Abd Al-Rahman Al-Ramhurmuzi said: Hammam told us, Ibrahim told us, from Al-Hasan, Na’il bin Nujayh told us, A’idh bin Habib told me, from Muhammad ibn Sa'id said: When Muhammad ibn Maslama al-Ansari died, we found written on the hilt of his sword: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “Indeed, your Lord has breezes in the remaining days of your life, so expose yourselves to Him, perhaps a supplication will coincide with mercy, and its owner will be blessed with a happiness after which he will never lose anything.” And the words of God, the Almighty: Indeed, those who are too arrogant to worship Me meaning to supplicate to Me and declare My Oneness will enter Hell in humiliation, that is, humiliated and contemptible, as Imam Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us from Ibn 'Ajlan, 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb narrated to me from his father, from his grandfather, from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “The arrogant will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection like ants in the form of people, with every kind of smallness above them, until they enter a prison in Hell called Bolus, with the fire of the flames above them, and they will be given to drink from the mud of corruption, the juice of the people of Hell.” Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali bin Al-Hussein told us, Abu Bakr bin Muhammad bin Yazid bin Khunais told us, he said: I heard my father narrating on the authority of Wahib bin Al-Ward, a man told me: I was walking one day in the land of the Romans and I heard a voice from the top of a mountain saying: O Lord, I am amazed at the one who knows You and how he can put his hope in anyone other than You. O Lord, I am amazed at the one who knows You and how he can seek his needs from anyone other than You. He said: Then it went away and then the greatest catastrophe came. He said: Then he came back a second time and said: O Lord, I am amazed at the one who knows You and how he can expose himself to any of Your wrath in order to please someone other than You. Wahib said: And this is the greatest catastrophe. He said: So I called out to him: Are you a human or a jinn? He said: Rather, I am a human. Occupy yourself with what concerns you and not with what does not concern you.
40:1: Interpretation of Surah Ghafir It is Meccan Some of the Salaf, including Muhammad ibn Sirin, disliked saying Al Ha Meem, but rather Al Ha Meem. Abdullah ibn Masoud may God be pleased with him said: Al Ha Meem is the brocade of the Quran. Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him said: Everything has a core, and the core of the Quran is Al Ha Meem, or he said Al Ha Meem. Misa’ar ibn Kadam said: They were called brides. The scholar and imam Abu Ubaid al-Qasim ibn Salam may God have mercy on him narrated all of that in his book The Virtues of the Quran. Humayd ibn Zanjawayh said: Ubaidullah ibn Musa told us, Isra’il told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu al-Ahwas, on the authority of Abdullah may God be pleased with him, who said: The example of the Quran is like that of a man who set out to look for a place to stay for his family, and he passed by the trail of rain. While he was walking and marveling at it, it descends upon soft meadows. He said, I am amazed at the first rain. This is even more marvelous. So it was said to him: The example of the first rain is like the greatness of the Quran, and these soft meadows are like Al Ha Meem in the Quran. Al-Baghawi included it. Ibn Lahi’ah said on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Habib that Al Jarrah ibn Abi Al Jarrah told him on the authority of Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them both who said: Everything has a core and the core of the Qur’an is the Ha Mim. Ibn Mas’ud may God be pleased with him said: When you come across Al Ha Mim, you have come to gardens in which I adorn myself. Abu Ubaid said: Al Ashja’i told us, Misa’ar told us - he is Ibn Kadam - on the authority of someone who told him that a man saw Abu Darda’ may God be pleased with him building a mosque, so he said to him: What is this? He said, I built it for the sake of the family of Ha Mim. This mosque, which was built by Abu Darda’ may God be pleased with him, may be the mosque attributed to him inside the Citadel of Damascus. It may also be that it was maintained and preserved by his blessing and the blessing of what it was built for, as these words indicate victory over the enemies, as the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to his companions during one of the battles: If you spend the night, say ‘Ha Mim’ and they will not be victorious. And in another narration: You will not be victorious. And Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar said, “Ahmad bin Al-Hakam bin Dhibyan bin Khalaf Al-Mazini and Muhammad bin Al-Layth Al-Hamadani told us, they said, Musa bin Masoud told us, Abdul-Rahman bin Abi Bakr Al-Maliki told us, on the authority of Zurarah bin Mus’ab, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurairah may God be pleased with him, who said, “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, ‘Whoever recites Ayat Al-Kursi and the beginning of Ha Mim Al-Mu’min will be protected that day from all evil.” Then he said, We do not know of it being narrated except with this chain of transmission. And Al-Tirmidhi narrated it from the hadith of Al-Maliki, and he said, Some scholars have criticized it because of its memory. In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful As for the discussion of the disconnected letters, it was presented at the beginning of Surat Al-Baqarah, so there is no need to repeat it here. It has been said that Ha Meem is one of the names of God Almighty, and they recited a verse about that: Ham reminds me of the spear, so why don't we fight before we advance? It was mentioned in the hadith narrated by Abu Dawud and Al-Tirmidhi on the authority of Al-Thawri on the authority of Abu Ishaq on the authority of Al-Muhallab bin Abi Sufrah, who said: I was told by someone who heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: If you spend the night, say ‘Ha Meem’ and they will not be helped. This is a sound chain of transmission. Abu Ubaid chose to narrate ‘say ‘Ha Meem’ and they will not be helped,’ meaning if you say that, they will not be helped, making it a reward for his saying ‘say.’” God the Almighty says: "The revelation of the Book is from God, the Exalted in Might, the Knowing." That is, the revelation of this Book, which is the Qur’an, is from God, the Possessor of Might and Knowledge. His presence is unapproachable, and not even an atom is hidden from Him, no matter how thick His veil is. God the Almighty says: "Forgiver of sin and Accepter of repentance." That is, He forgives past sins and accepts repentance in the future for whoever repents to Him and submits to Him. God the Almighty says: "Severe in penalty." That is, for whoever rebels, transgresses, prefers worldly life, defies God’s commands, and transgresses. This is similar to His saying: "Inform My servants that it is I who am the Forgiving, the Merciful, and that it is My punishment that is the painful punishment." These two descriptions are often combined in various places in the Qur’an to keep the servant between hope and fear. God the Almighty says: "Possessor of bounty." Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him said that it means abundance and riches. Mujahid and Qatadah said the same. Yazid ibn al-Asam said that "Possessor of bounty" means abundant good. Ikrimah said that "Possessor of bounty means Possessor of grace." Qatada said: The Possessor of blessings and bounties, meaning that He is the One who is generous to His servants and is lenient with them with what they have of favors and blessings that they cannot even be able to thank even a single one of them. And if you should count the favors of God, you could not enumerate them (al-An’am 2:17). And His statement, may He be glorified and exalted: There is no deity except Him means that He has no equal in all of His attributes, there is no god but Him, there is no god or lord but Him. To Him is the final destination means the return and the final destination, so He will reward every worker according to his work. And He is Swift in account. Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash said: I heard Abu Ishaq al-Subai’i say: A man came to Umar ibn al-Khattab may God be pleased with him and said: O Commander of the Faithful, I have been killed, so is there any repentance for me? Umar may God be pleased with him recited: “Ha Meem. The revelation of the Book is from God, the Exalted in Might, the Knowing. The Forgiver of sin and Accepter of repentance, Severe in penalty” (al-An’am 2:17). Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim: And the wording is his, and Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Musa ibn Marwan al-Raqi told us, Umar - meaning Ibn Ayyub - told us, Jaafar ibn Burqan told us, on the authority of Yazid ibn al-Asam, who said: There was a man from the people of Ash-Sham who was a man of valor, and he used to visit Umar ibn al-Khattab may God be pleased with him. Umar missed him, so he said: What has happened to so-and-so ibn so-and-so? They said: O Commander of the Faithful, you keep drinking this drink. So Umar called his scribe and said: Write from Umar ibn al-Khattab to so-and-so ibn so-and-so: Peace be upon you, for I praise to you God, there is no god but Him, the Forgiver of sin, the Accepter of repentance, the Severe in punishment, the Possessor of bounty, there is no god but Him, to Him is the final destination. Then he said to his companions: Ask God for your brother to accept his heart and accept his repentance. When the man received Umar’s letter may God be pleased with him, he began to read it and repeat it, saying: Forgiver of sin, Accepter of repentance, Severe in punishment, He has warned me of His punishment and promised to forgive me. Al-Hafiz Abu Naim narrated it from the hadith of Ja`far ibn Burqan, and he added: He kept repeating it to himself, then he cried, then he died and died well. When Umar heard about it, he said: This is what you should do if you see a brother of yours slipping up. Correct him, support him, and pray to God to accept his repentance, and do not be helpers of Satan against him. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Omar bin Shaiba told us, Hammad bin Waqid told us, Abu Omar Al-Saffar told us, Thabit Al-Banani told us, he said: I was with Mus`ab bin Al-Zubayr, may God be pleased with him, in the open plains of Kufa. I entered an enclosure to pray two rak`ahs, and I began to recite Ha Mim Al-Mu`min until I reached: There is no god but He, to Him is the final destination. Then a man came behind me on a gray mule with Yemeni patches on him. He said: When you say: Forgiver of sin, then say: O Forgiver of sin, forgive my sin. And when you say: Accepter of repentance, then say: O Accepter of repentance, accept my repentance. And when you say: Severe in punishment, then say: O Severe in punishment, do not punish me. He said: I turned around and did not see anyone, so I went out to the door and said: A man passed by you with Yemeni patches on him. They said: We did not see anyone. They thought that he was Elias. Then he narrated it from another chain of transmission on the authority of Thabit in a similar manner, but it did not mention Elias. And God Almighty knows best.
40:2: As for the discussion of the disconnected letters, it was presented at the beginning of Surat Al-Baqarah, so there is no need to repeat it here. It has been said that Ha Meem is one of the names of God Almighty, and they recited a verse about that: Ham reminds me of the spear, so why don't we fight before we advance? It was mentioned in the hadith narrated by Abu Dawud and Al-Tirmidhi on the authority of Al-Thawri on the authority of Abu Ishaq on the authority of Al-Muhallab bin Abi Sufrah, who said: I was told by someone who heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: If you spend the night, say ‘Ha Meem’ and they will not be helped. This is a sound chain of transmission. Abu Ubaid chose to narrate ‘say ‘Ha Meem’ and they will not be helped,’ meaning if you say that, they will not be helped, making it a reward for his saying ‘say.’” God the Almighty says: The revelation of the Book is from God, the Exalted in Might, the Knowing. That is, the revelation of this Book, which is the Qur’an, is from God, the Possessor of Might and Knowledge. His presence is unapproachable, and not even an atom is hidden from Him, no matter how thick His veil is. God the Almighty says: Forgiver of sin and Accepter of repentance. That is, He forgives past sins and accepts repentance in the future for whoever repents to Him and submits to Him. God the Almighty says: Severe in penalty. That is, for whoever rebels, transgresses, prefers worldly life, defies God’s commands, and transgresses. This is similar to His saying: Inform My servants that it is I who am the Forgiving, the Merciful, and that it is My punishment that is the painful punishment. These two descriptions are often combined in various places in the Qur’an to keep the servant between hope and fear. God the Almighty says: Possessor of bounty. Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him said that it means abundance and riches. Mujahid and Qatadah said the same. Yazid ibn al-Asam said that Possessor of bounty means abundant good. Ikrimah said that Possessor of bounty means Possessor of grace. Qatada said: The Possessor of blessings and bounties, meaning that He is the One who is generous to His servants and is lenient with them with what they have of favors and blessings that they cannot even be able to thank even a single one of them. And if you should count the favors of God, you could not enumerate them (al-An’am 2:17). And His statement, may He be glorified and exalted: There is no deity except Him means that He has no equal in all of His attributes, there is no god but Him, there is no god or lord but Him. To Him is the final destination means the return and the final destination, so He will reward every worker according to his work. And He is Swift in account. Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash said: I heard Abu Ishaq al-Subai’i say: A man came to Umar ibn al-Khattab may God be pleased with him and said: O Commander of the Faithful, I have been killed, so is there any repentance for me? Umar may God be pleased with him recited: “Ha Meem. The revelation of the Book is from God, the Exalted in Might, the Knowing. The Forgiver of sin and Accepter of repentance, Severe in penalty” (al-An’am 2:17). Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim: And the wording is his, and Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Musa ibn Marwan al-Raqi told us, Umar - meaning Ibn Ayyub - told us, Jaafar ibn Burqan told us, on the authority of Yazid ibn al-Asam, who said: There was a man from the people of Ash-Sham who was a man of valor, and he used to visit Umar ibn al-Khattab may God be pleased with him. Umar missed him, so he said: What has happened to so-and-so ibn so-and-so? They said: O Commander of the Faithful, you keep drinking this drink. So Umar called his scribe and said: Write from Umar ibn al-Khattab to so-and-so ibn so-and-so: Peace be upon you, for I praise to you God, there is no god but Him, the Forgiver of sin, the Accepter of repentance, the Severe in punishment, the Possessor of bounty, there is no god but Him, to Him is the final destination. Then he said to his companions: Ask God for your brother to accept his heart and accept his repentance. When the man received Umar’s letter may God be pleased with him, he began to read it and repeat it, saying: Forgiver of sin, Accepter of repentance, Severe in punishment, He has warned me of His punishment and promised to forgive me. Al-Hafiz Abu Naim narrated it from the hadith of Ja`far ibn Burqan, and he added: He kept repeating it to himself, then he cried, then he died and died well. When Umar heard about it, he said: This is what you should do if you see a brother of yours slipping up. Correct him, support him, and pray to God to accept his repentance, and do not be helpers of Satan against him. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Omar bin Shaiba told us, Hammad bin Waqid told us, Abu Omar Al-Saffar told us, Thabit Al-Banani told us, he said: I was with Mus`ab bin Al-Zubayr, may God be pleased with him, in the open plains of Kufa. I entered an enclosure to pray two rak`ahs, and I began to recite Ha Mim Al-Mu`min until I reached: There is no god but He, to Him is the final destination. Then a man came behind me on a gray mule with Yemeni patches on him. He said: When you say: Forgiver of sin, then say: O Forgiver of sin, forgive my sin. And when you say: Accepter of repentance, then say: O Accepter of repentance, accept my repentance. And when you say: Severe in punishment, then say: O Severe in punishment, do not punish me. He said: I turned around and did not see anyone, so I went out to the door and said: A man passed by you with Yemeni patches on him. They said: We did not see anyone. They thought that he was Elias. Then he narrated it from another chain of transmission on the authority of Thabit in a similar manner, but it did not mention Elias. And God Almighty knows best.

40:4: God Almighty says that what is denied and disputed after the clarification and the appearance of the proof except those who disbelieve meaning those who deny the signs, proofs and evidence of God so let not their movement in the lands deceive you meaning in its wealth, comforts and prosperity as God Almighty said: Let not the movement of those who disbelieve in the lands deceive you * A brief enjoyment; then their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the resting place. And God Almighty said: We grant them enjoyment for a little; then We will force them to a severe punishment. Then God Almighty said, consoling His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, in denying those of his people who denied him, that he had an example in those prophets who came before him, peace and blessings be upon them, for their nations denied them and opposed them, and only a few of them believed in them. He said: The people of Noah denied before them he was the first messenger sent by God to forbid the worship of idols and the parties after them meaning from every nation and every nation plotted against their messenger to seize him meaning They were keen to kill him by all possible means, and some of them killed his Messenger. And they argued with falsehood to refute thereby the truth, meaning they used doubt to reject the clear and obvious truth. Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Ali ibn Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, Arim Abu al-Nu’man narrated to us, Mu’tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, he said: I heard my father narrating, on the authority of Hanash, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever aids falsehood in order to refute the truth, then the responsibility of God and the responsibility of His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, is void of him.” And His, the Most High, saying: So I seized them means I destroyed them for what they had done of these grave sins and transgressions. Then how was My punishment? means how did My punishment and chastisement of them reach you? It was severe, painful and agonizing. Qatadah said: It was severe, by God. And His, the Most High, saying: And thus the word of your Lord has come into effect upon those who disbelieved, that they are companions of the Fire means, just as the word of punishment came into effect upon those who disbelieved among the previous nations, so it came into effect upon the deniers among these who denied you and opposed you, O Muhammad, by a fortiori and more appropriate way, because whoever denies you cannot be trusted to believe anyone other than you, and God knows best.

40:7: God the Almighty tells us about the angels close to Him, the four bearers of the Throne and the Cherubim around Him, that they glorify their Lord with praise, that is, they combine glorification, which indicates the negation of shortcomings, with praise, which requires establishing the attributes of praise. And they believe in Him, that is, they are humble before Him and submissive before Him, and that they ask forgiveness for those who believe, that is, from the people of the earth who believed in the unseen. So God the Almighty appointed His angels close to Him to supplicate for the believers in their absence, as proven in Sahih Muslim: When a Muslim supplicates for his brother in his absence, the angel says, ‘Amen, and for you the same.’ Imam Ahmad said: Abdullah ibn Muhammad, who is Ibn Abi Shabiya, narrated to us, ‘Abdah ibn Sulayman, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Ya’qub ibn ‘Utbah, on the authority of ‘Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn ‘Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Umayyah ibn Abi Salt spoke the truth in some of his poetry. So he said: Saturn and Taurus under his right foot, and the eagle under the other, and Leith the observatory The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: He is telling the truth. He said: And the sun rises every last night, red and its color turns rosy She refuses, and she does not send us any of her messengers except to punish or flog. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: He has spoken the truth. This is a good chain of transmission and it indicates that the bearers of the Throne today are four, but if it is the Day of Resurrection they will be eight, as God the Almighty said: And eight will bear the Throne of your Lord above them that Day. Here is a question: How can we reconcile the meaning of this verse and the significance of this hadith? And between the hadith narrated by Abu Dawud: Muhammad ibn al-Sabah al-Bazzar told us, al-Walid ibn Abi Thawr told us, from Samak, from Abdullah ibn Umayrah, from al-Ahnaf ibn Qays, from al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib may God be pleased with him, who said: I was in al-Batha’ with a group among whom was the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), and a cloud passed by them. He looked at it and said: What do you call this? They said: The clouds. He said: And the rain clouds. They said: And the rain clouds. He said: And the reins. Abu Dawud said: I did not understand the reins well. He said: Do you know how far is between the heaven and the earth? They said, We do not know. He said, “Between them is either one, two, or three years. Then the sky is above it like that until he counted seven heavens. Then above the seventh sky is a sea, between its bottom and its top is like the distance between one heaven and the next. Then above that are eight mountain goats, between their hooves and their knees is like the distance between one heaven and the next. Then on their backs is the Throne, between its bottom and its top is like the distance between one heaven and the next. Then God, Blessed and Exalted is He, is above that.” Then Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of Samak bin Harb with it, and Al-Tirmidhi said: It is hasan gharib. This indicates that the bearers of the Throne are eight, as Shahr bin Hawshab, may God be pleased with him, said: The bearers of the Throne are eight: Four of them say: Glory be to You, O God, and praise be to You. To You be praise for Your forbearance after Your knowledge. And four of them say: Glory be to You, O God, and praise be to You. To You be praise for Your forgiveness after Your power. And for this reason they say when they seek forgiveness for those who have believed: Our Lord, You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge. That is, Your mercy encompasses their sins and transgressions, and Your knowledge encompasses all their deeds, words, movements and stillness. So forgive those who have repented and followed Your way. That is, pardon the wrongdoers if they repent, return, desist from what they were doing and follow what You have commanded them to do of doing good and abandoning evil. And protect them from the punishment of Hellfire. That is, and remove them from the punishment of Hellfire, which is the painful, agonizing punishment. Our Lord, and admit them to the Gardens of Eden which You have promised them and whoever was righteous among their fathers, their spouses and their offspring. That is, unite them and them. So that their eyes may be comforted by meeting in adjacent dwellings, as God the Most High said: And those who have believed and whose offspring followed them in faith - We will join with them their offspring and not deprive them of anything of their deeds. That is, We made everyone equal in status so that their eyes may be comforted. We did not diminish the high in order to equal the low. Rather, We raised those who were deficient in deeds and made them equal to those who did much good, as a favor and grace from Us. Sa’id ibn Jubayr said: When a believer enters Paradise, he will be asked about his father, son, and brother, where they are. It will be said: They did not reach your level in deeds. He will say: I only worked for myself and for them. So they will join him in degree. Then Sa’id ibn Jubayr recited this verse: “Our Lord, and admit them to Gardens of Eden which You have promised them - and whoever was righteous among their fathers, their spouses, and their offspring. Indeed, it is You who is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.” Mutraf ibn Abdullah ibn Ash-Shakheer said: The angels advise God’s servants to the believers. Then he recited this verse: Our Lord, and admit them to Gardens of Eden which You have promised them. And the devils deceive His servants to the believers. And the saying of the Blessed and Exalted: Indeed, You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise meaning the One who is not prevented or overcome. Whatever He wills will be, and whatever He does not will will not be. The Wise in Your words and actions is from Your law and decree. And protect them from evil deeds meaning their commission or the consequences of them from whomever they occur. And whomever You protect from evil deeds on that Day meaning the Day of Resurrection You have had mercy on him meaning You have been kind to him and saved him from punishment. And that is the great attainment.

Then Sa’id ibn Jubayr recited this verse: “Our Lord, and admit them to Gardens of Eden which You have promised them - and whoever was righteous among their fathers, their spouses, and their offspring. Indeed, it is You who is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.” Mutraf ibn Abdullah ibn Ash-Shakheer said: The angels advise God’s servants to the believers. Then he recited this verse: Our Lord, and admit them to Gardens of Eden which You have promised them. And the devils deceive His servants to the believers. And the saying of the Blessed and Exalted: Indeed, You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise meaning the One who is not prevented or overcome. Whatever He wills will be, and whatever He does not will will not be. The Wise in Your words and actions is from Your law and decree. And protect them from evil deeds meaning their commission or the consequences of them from whomever they occur. And whomever You protect from evil deeds on that Day meaning the Day of Resurrection You have had mercy on him meaning You have been kind to him and saved him from punishment. And that is the great attainment.
40:9: God the Almighty tells us about the angels close to Him, the four bearers of the Throne and the Cherubim around Him, that they glorify their Lord with praise, that is, they combine glorification, which indicates the negation of shortcomings, with praise, which requires establishing the attributes of praise. And they believe in Him, that is, they are humble before Him and submissive before Him, and that they ask forgiveness for those who believe, that is, from the people of the earth who believed in the unseen. So God the Almighty appointed His angels close to Him to supplicate for the believers in their absence, as proven in Sahih Muslim: When a Muslim supplicates for his brother in his absence, the angel says, ‘Amen, and for you the same.’ Imam Ahmad said: Abdullah ibn Muhammad, who is Ibn Abi Shabiya, narrated to us, ‘Abdah ibn Sulayman, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Ya’qub ibn ‘Utbah, on the authority of ‘Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn ‘Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Umayyah ibn Abi Salt spoke the truth in some of his poetry. So he said: Saturn and Taurus under his right foot, and the eagle under the other, and Leith the observatory The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: He is telling the truth. He said: And the sun rises every last night, red and its color turns rosy She refuses, and she does not send us any of her messengers except to punish or flog. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: He has spoken the truth. This is a good chain of transmission and it indicates that the bearers of the Throne today are four, but if it is the Day of Resurrection they will be eight, as God the Almighty said: And eight will bear the Throne of your Lord above them that Day. Here is a question: How can we reconcile the meaning of this verse and the significance of this hadith? And between the hadith narrated by Abu Dawud: Muhammad ibn al-Sabah al-Bazzar told us, al-Walid ibn Abi Thawr told us, from Samak, from Abdullah ibn Umayrah, from al-Ahnaf ibn Qays, from al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib may God be pleased with him, who said: I was in al-Batha’ with a group among whom was the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), and a cloud passed by them. He looked at it and said: What do you call this? They said: The clouds. He said: And the rain clouds. They said: And the rain clouds. He said: And the reins. Abu Dawud said: I did not understand the reins well. He said: Do you know how far is between the heaven and the earth? They said, We do not know. He said, “Between them is either one, two, or three years. Then the sky is above it like that until he counted seven heavens. Then above the seventh sky is a sea, between its bottom and its top is like the distance between one heaven and the next. Then above that are eight mountain goats, between their hooves and their knees is like the distance between one heaven and the next. Then on their backs is the Throne, between its bottom and its top is like the distance between one heaven and the next. Then God, Blessed and Exalted is He, is above that.” Then Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of Samak bin Harb with it, and Al-Tirmidhi said: It is hasan gharib. This indicates that the bearers of the Throne are eight, as Shahr bin Hawshab, may God be pleased with him, said: The bearers of the Throne are eight: Four of them say: Glory be to You, O God, and praise be to You. To You be praise for Your forbearance after Your knowledge. And four of them say: Glory be to You, O God, and praise be to You. To You be praise for Your forgiveness after Your power. And for this reason they say when they seek forgiveness for those who have believed: Our Lord, You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge. That is, Your mercy encompasses their sins and transgressions, and Your knowledge encompasses all their deeds, words, movements and stillness. So forgive those who have repented and followed Your way. That is, pardon the wrongdoers if they repent, return, desist from what they were doing and follow what You have commanded them to do of doing good and abandoning evil. And protect them from the punishment of Hellfire. That is, and remove them from the punishment of Hellfire, which is the painful, agonizing punishment. Our Lord, and admit them to the Gardens of Eden which You have promised them and whoever was righteous among their fathers, their spouses and their offspring. That is, unite them and them. So that their eyes may be comforted by meeting in adjacent dwellings, as God the Most High said: And those who have believed and whose offspring followed them in faith - We will join with them their offspring and not deprive them of anything of their deeds. That is, We made everyone equal in status so that their eyes may be comforted. We did not diminish the high in order to equal the low. Rather, We raised those who were deficient in deeds and made them equal to those who did much good, as a favor and grace from Us. Sa’id ibn Jubayr said: When a believer enters Paradise, he will be asked about his father, son, and brother, where they are. It will be said: They did not reach your level in deeds. He will say: I only worked for myself and for them. So they will join him in degree. Then Sa’id ibn Jubayr recited this verse: “Our Lord, and admit them to Gardens of Eden which You have promised them - and whoever was righteous among their fathers, their spouses, and their offspring. Indeed, it is You who is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.” Mutraf ibn Abdullah ibn Ash-Shakheer said: The angels advise God’s servants to the believers. Then he recited this verse: Our Lord, and admit them to Gardens of Eden which You have promised them. And the devils deceive His servants to the believers. And the saying of the Blessed and Exalted: Indeed, You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise meaning the One who is not prevented or overcome. Whatever He wills will be, and whatever He does not will will not be. The Wise in Your words and actions is from Your law and decree. And protect them from evil deeds meaning their commission or the consequences of them from whomever they occur. And whomever You protect from evil deeds on that Day meaning the Day of Resurrection You have had mercy on him meaning You have been kind to him and saved him from punishment. And that is the great attainment.
40:10: God the Almighty says, informing us about the disbelievers that they will be called on the Day of Resurrection while they are engulfed in the blazing Fire, when they are directly exposed to a punishment from God that no one can bear. They will then detest and loathe themselves terribly because of the evil deeds they did that caused them to enter the Fire. Then the angels will inform them, calling out to them, that God's hatred for them in this world when He offered them faith and they disbelieved is greater than your hatred of yourselves today, O you who are being tormented. Qatada said about God's statement: {The hatred of God is greater than your hatred of yourselves when you were called to faith and you disbelieved}. He means that God's hatred of the people of misguidance when faith was offered to them in this world and they abandoned it and refused to accept it is greater than their hatred of themselves when they witnessed God's punishment on the Day of Resurrection. This is what Al-Hasan Al-Basri, Mujahid, Al-Suddi, Dhirr ibn Ubaydullah Al-Hamdani, Abd Al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, and Ibn Jarir Al-Tabari, may God have mercy on them all, said. And His statement: They said, ‘Our Lord, You caused us to die twice and You gave us life twice.’ Al-Thawri said on the authority of Abu Ishaq on the authority of Abu Al-Ahwas on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, may God be pleased with him, that this verse is like the statement of God Almighty: How can you disbelieve in God while you were dead and He gave you life? Then He will cause you to die, then He will bring you to life, and then to Him you will be returned. Ibn Abbas, Al-Dahhak, Qatadah, and Abu Malik said the same. This is the correct statement about which there is no doubt or uncertainty. Al-Suddi said: They were killed in this world, then revived in their graves, and they were addressed, then they were killed, then revived on the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Zayd said: They were revived when the covenant was taken from them from the loins of Adam, peace be upon him, then He created them in the wombs, then He caused them to die, then He revived them on the Day of Resurrection. These two statements from Al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd are weak because, according to what they said, they require three resurrections and three deaths. The correct statement is that of Ibn Masoud, Ibn Abbas, and those who followed them. The point of all of this is that the disbelievers ask to return while they are standing before God Almighty on the Day of Resurrection, as God Almighty said: “And if you could but see when the guilty will hang their heads before their Lord, [saying], ‘Our Lord, we have seen and heard, so return us [to the world]; we will work righteousness. Indeed, we are [now] certain.” But they will not be answered. Then when they see the Fire and witness it and stand before it and look at the torment and punishment in it, they will ask to return more severely than they asked the first time, but they will not be answered. God Almighty said: “And if you could but see when they are made to stand before the Fire and say, ‘Oh, would that we could be sent back and not be denied. ’” By the signs of our Lord, and we will be among the believers. * Rather, what they concealed before will become apparent to them. And if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden, and indeed, they are liars. "So when they enter the Fire and taste its touch and its hissing and its whips and its shackles, their request to return will be more severe and greater. "And they will cry out therein, "Our Lord, take us out; we will do righteousness other than what we used to do. Did We not give you life long enough for whoever would remember therein to remember? And a warner has come to you, so taste [this [revelation]; for there is no helper for the wrongdoers." "Our Lord, take us out of it. If we return, then we are wrongdoers." * He will say, Remain despised therein and do not speak to [others]. In this noble verse, they were gentle in their question and presented an introduction to their speech, which is their saying, Our Lord, You caused us to die twice and You gave us life twice. That is, Your power is great, for You gave us life after we were dead, then You caused us to die, then You gave us life. You are able to do whatever You will. We have acknowledged our sins and that we were wrongdoers to ourselves in this world. So is there any way out? That is, will You answer us until You return us to this world? Able to do so, so that we may do other than what we were doing. If we return to what we were in, then we are wrongdoers. So respond that there is no way for you to return and return to the worldly home. Then He explained the prevention of that by saying that your natures do not accept the truth nor require it, but rather deny and reject it. For this reason, the Almighty said: That is because when God alone is called upon, you disbelieve, and if partners are associated with Him, you believe. That is, this is how you will be even if you are returned to the worldly home, as the Almighty said: And if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden, and indeed, they are liars. And the Almighty said: The judgment belongs to God, the Most High, the Great. That is, He is the Judge over His creation, the Just, who does not act unjustly. He guides whomever He wills and misguides whomever He wills, and has mercy on whomever He wills and punishes whomever He wills. There is no god but Him. And the Almighty said: It is He who shows you His signs. That is, He demonstrates His power to His creation through what they see in His creation, both higher and lower, of the great signs that indicate the perfection of its Creator, Initiator and Originator. And He sends down for you provision from the sky. That is, the rain that comes out. From the crops and fruits there is what is seen by the senses in terms of the difference in their colors, tastes, smells, shapes and colors, and it is one water. So by the great power He made a distinction between these things. And none will remember that is, consider and reflect on these things and use them as evidence of the greatness of their Creator. Except he who turns back that is, he who is perceptive and turns back to God Almighty. And the Almighty’s saying: So call upon God, devoting your religion to Him, even though the disbelievers hate it that is, be sincere in your worship and supplication to God alone and differ from the polytheists in their conduct and doctrine. Imam Ahmad said: Abdullah bin Numayr told us, Hisham, meaning bin Urwah bin Az-Zubayr, told us, on the authority of Abu Az-Zubayr Muhammad bin Muslim bin Mudarris Al-Makki, who said: Abdullah bin Az-Zubayr used to say after every prayer when he finished the salutation: “There is no god but God alone, with no partner. His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He has power over all things. There is no power nor strength save with God. There is no god but God, and we do not worship except Him. His is the blessing and His is the bounty and His is the best praise. There is no god but God, making our religion sincere to Him, even if the disbelievers hate it.” He said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) used to say these words after every prayer. Muslim, Abu Dawud, and An-Nasa’i narrated it through various chains of narration on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah, Hajjaj bin Abi Uthman, and Musa bin Uqbah, all three of them on the authority of Abu Az-Zubayr, on the authority of Abdullah bin Az-Zubayr, who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) used to say after every prayer: There is no god but God alone, with no partner. And he mentioned the rest of it. It was proven in Sahih Al-Bukhari on the authority of Ibn Al-Zubayr may God be pleased with him that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to say after the obligatory prayers: “There is no god but God alone, with no partner. His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He has power over all things. There is no might nor power except with God. There is no god but God, and we worship none but Him. His is the blessing and His is the bounty and His is the good praise. There is no god but God, devoting our religion to Him, even though the disbelievers hate it.” Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Rabi’ told us, Al-Khasib bin Nasi’ told us, Salih - meaning Al-Murri - told us, on the authority of Hisham bin Hassan, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, on the authority of Abu Hurairah may God be pleased with him, that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Call upon God, the Blessed and Exalted, and be certain of a response, and know that God does not answer the supplication of a heedless, distracted heart.

40:14: God the Almighty says, informing us about the disbelievers that they will be called on the Day of Resurrection while they are engulfed in the blazing Fire, when they are directly exposed to a punishment from God that no one can bear. They will then detest and loathe themselves terribly because of the evil deeds they did that caused them to enter the Fire. Then the angels will inform them, calling out to them, that God's hatred for them in this world when He offered them faith and they disbelieved is greater than your hatred of yourselves today, O you who are being tormented. Qatada said about God's statement: {The hatred of God is greater than your hatred of yourselves when you were called to faith and you disbelieved}. He means that God's hatred of the people of misguidance when faith was offered to them in this world and they abandoned it and refused to accept it is greater than their hatred of themselves when they witnessed God's punishment on the Day of Resurrection. This is what Al-Hasan Al-Basri, Mujahid, Al-Suddi, Dhirr ibn Ubaydullah Al-Hamdani, Abd Al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, and Ibn Jarir Al-Tabari, may God have mercy on them all, said. And His statement: They said, ‘Our Lord, You caused us to die twice and You gave us life twice.’ Al-Thawri said on the authority of Abu Ishaq on the authority of Abu Al-Ahwas on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, may God be pleased with him, that this verse is like the statement of God Almighty: How can you disbelieve in God while you were dead and He gave you life? Then He will cause you to die, then He will bring you to life, and then to Him you will be returned. Ibn Abbas, Al-Dahhak, Qatadah, and Abu Malik said the same. This is the correct statement about which there is no doubt or uncertainty. Al-Suddi said: They were killed in this world, then revived in their graves, and they were addressed, then they were killed, then revived on the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Zayd said: They were revived when the covenant was taken from them from the loins of Adam, peace be upon him, then He created them in the wombs, then He caused them to die, then He revived them on the Day of Resurrection. These two statements from Al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd are weak because, according to what they said, they require three resurrections and three deaths. The correct statement is that of Ibn Masoud, Ibn Abbas, and those who followed them. The point of all of this is that the disbelievers ask to return while they are standing before God Almighty on the Day of Resurrection, as God Almighty said: “And if you could but see when the guilty will hang their heads before their Lord, [saying], ‘Our Lord, we have seen and heard, so return us [to the world]; we will work righteousness. Indeed, we are [now] certain.” But they will not be answered. Then when they see the Fire and witness it and stand before it and look at the torment and punishment in it, they will ask to return more severely than they asked the first time, but they will not be answered. God Almighty said: “And if you could but see when they are made to stand before the Fire and say, ‘Oh, would that we could be sent back and not be denied. ’” By the signs of our Lord, and we will be among the believers. * Rather, what they concealed before will become apparent to them. And if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden, and indeed, they are liars. "So when they enter the Fire and taste its touch and its hissing and its whips and its shackles, their request to return will be more severe and greater. "And they will cry out therein, "Our Lord, take us out; we will do righteousness other than what we used to do. Did We not give you life long enough for whoever would remember therein to remember? And a warner has come to you, so taste [this [revelation]; for there is no helper for the wrongdoers." "Our Lord, take us out of it. If we return, then we are wrongdoers." * He will say, Remain despised therein and do not speak to [others]. In this noble verse, they were gentle in their question and presented an introduction to their speech, which is their saying, Our Lord, You caused us to die twice and You gave us life twice. That is, Your power is great, for You gave us life after we were dead, then You caused us to die, then You gave us life. You are able to do whatever You will. We have acknowledged our sins and that we were wrongdoers to ourselves in this world. So is there any way out? That is, will You answer us until You return us to this world? Able to do so, so that we may do other than what we were doing. If we return to what we were in, then we are wrongdoers. So respond that there is no way for you to return and return to the worldly home. Then He explained the prevention of that by saying that your natures do not accept the truth nor require it, but rather deny and reject it. For this reason, the Almighty said: That is because when God alone is called upon, you disbelieve, and if partners are associated with Him, you believe. That is, this is how you will be even if you are returned to the worldly home, as the Almighty said: And if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden, and indeed, they are liars. He guides whomever He wills and misguides whomever He wills, and has mercy on whomever He wills and punishes whomever He wills. There is no god but Him. And the Almighty said: It is He who shows you His signs. That is, He demonstrates His power to His creation through what they see in His creation, both higher and lower, of the great signs that indicate the perfection of its Creator, Initiator and Originator. And He sends down for you provision from the sky. That is, the rain that comes out. From the crops and fruits there is what is seen by the senses in terms of the difference in their colors, tastes, smells, shapes and colors, and it is one water. So by the great power He made a distinction between these things. And none will remember that is, consider and reflect on these things and use them as evidence of the greatness of their Creator. Except he who turns back that is, he who is perceptive and turns back to God Almighty. 40:15: The Almighty says, informing about His greatness, pride, and the height of His great and lofty throne above all His creations, like a roof over them, as He the Almighty said: “From God, Lord of the Ascending Stairways. The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him during a Day the extent of which is fifty thousand years.” And there will come, God willing, an explanation that this is the distance between the throne and the seventh earth, according to a group of the early and later generations, and this is the most likely, God willing. And more than one person has mentioned that the throne is made of red ruby, and the width between its two diagonals is a journey of fifty thousand years. And its height above the seventh earth is a journey of fifty thousand years. And we have already mentioned in the hadith of the mountain goats what indicates its height above the seven heavens by a great amount. God the Almighty says: He sends down the spirit by His command upon whom He wills of His servants, just as He the Almighty says: He sends down the angels with the spirit by His command upon whom He wills of His servants, [saying], ‘Warn that there is no deity except Me, so fear Me.’ And He the Almighty says: “And indeed, it is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds. * The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down * Upon your heart that you may be among the warners.” For this reason, God the Almighty said: To warn of the Day of Meeting. Ali ibn Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The Day of Meeting is one of the names of the Day of Resurrection from which God has warned His servants. Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him said: Adam and the last of his children will meet on it. Ibn Zayd said: The servants will meet on it. Qatadah, As-Suddi, Bilal ibn Sa’d, and Sufyan ibn Uyaynah said: The people of the heavens and the earth, the Creator and the creation, will meet on it. Maymun ibn Mihran said: The oppressor and the oppressed will meet. It may be said that the Day of Meeting includes all of this and that every worker will be met for what he has done of good and evil, as others have said. And His statement, the Most High: The Day they will come forth, nothing of them will be hidden from God, meaning they will be apparent and visible, all of them, nothing will conceal them, shade them, or cover them. That is why He said: The Day they will come forth, nothing of them will be hidden from God, meaning everyone is equally in His knowledge. And His statement, the Blessed and Exalted: Whose is the dominion this Day? To God, the One, the Prevailing, has been mentioned previously in the hadith of Ibn Umar may God be pleased with him that God, the Most High, will fold the heavens and the earth with His hand, then say, “I am the King, I am the Compeller, I am the Arrogant. Where are the kings of the earth? Where are the compellers? Where are the arrogant ones?” And in the hadith of the trumpet, it is stated that when He, the Almighty, takes the souls of all His creation, leaving none but Him alone, with no partner, then He will say, To whom belongs the dominion this Day? three times. Then He will answer Himself, saying, To God, the One, the Prevailing, meaning He alone has subdued and overcome all things. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad bin Ghaleb Al-Daqqaq told us, Ubaid bin Ubaidah told us, Mu’tamir told us, on the authority of his father, Abu Nadra told us, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: A caller will call out before the Hour: O people, the Hour has come upon you. The living and the dead will hear it. He said: Then God Almighty will descend to the lowest heaven and say: To whom belongs the kingdom this Day? To God, the One, the Prevailing. And His saying, may He be glorified: “This Day every soul will be recompensed for what it has earned. There is no injustice today. Indeed, God is swift in account.” God, the Most High, informs us of His justice in His judgment among His creation, that He does not wrong by an atom’s weight of good or evil, but rather He rewards for a good deed tenfold and for a bad deed once. God, the Most Blessed, the Most High, said: There is no injustice today, as is established in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Abu Dharr, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, in what he narrates from his Lord, the Almighty, that He said: “O My servants, I have forbidden injustice for Myself and made it forbidden amongst you, so do not wrong one another—until He said—O My servants, it is only your deeds that I count against you and then recompense you for. So whoever finds good, let him praise God, the Blessed and Most High, and whoever finds otherwise, let him blame no one but himself.” And His saying, the Almighty, the Most High: Indeed, God is swift in account, means that He will hold all of creation to account just as He holds a single soul to account, as He, the Most High, said: He did not create you and resurrect you except as a single soul. And He, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious, said: And Our command is but one. In the blink of an eye.

40:18: The Day of Approaching is one of the names of the Day of Resurrection. It was named thus because of its nearness, as God the Almighty said: “The approaching hour has drawn near. There is none to avert it but God.” And He the Almighty said: The Hour has drawn near, and the moon has split. And He the Almighty said: The reckoning of the people has drawn near. And He the Almighty said: The Command of God has come, so do not hasten it. And He the Almighty said: But when they see it approaching, the faces of those who disbelieved will be darkened. And God the Almighty said: When the hearts will be at the throats, stifling. Qatadah said: The hearts will stop in the throats out of fear, neither coming out nor returning to their places. This is what Ikrimah, As-Suddi and others said. The meaning of stifling is silent, no one will speak except with His permission. The Day the Spirit and the angels will stand in rows, none will speak except he whom the Most Merciful permits, and he will say what is right. Ibn Jurayj said: Stifling means weeping. God the Almighty says: For the wrongdoers there will be neither a close friend nor an intercessor whose intercession will be obeyed. That is, those who wronged themselves by associating partners with God will not have anyone close to them who could benefit them, nor an intercessor who could intercede for them. Rather, all means of good have been cut off from them. God the Almighty says: He knows the treachery of the eyes and what the breasts conceal. God the Almighty informs us of His perfect knowledge that encompasses all things, great and small, big and small, minute and subtle, so that people may beware of His knowledge of them, be truly ashamed before God the Almighty, fear Him the way He should be feared, and watch Him as one knows that he sees Him. Indeed, He the Almighty knows the treacherous eye, even if it displays honesty, and He knows what the secrets and inner thoughts of the breasts conceal. Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him said regarding the verse {He knows the deceit of the eyes and what the breasts conceal}, it is a man who enters a house while there is a beautiful woman among them, or he passes by while there is a beautiful woman among them. If they are not paying attention, he glances at her, but when they realize, he lowers his gaze. If they are not paying attention, he glances, but when they realize, he lowers his gaze. God has seen from his heart that he wishes he could look at her private parts. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Ad-Dahhak said, The deceit of the eyes is winking, and a man saying, I saw when he did not see, or I did not see when he saw. Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him said, God knows from the eye in its glance whether it intends to betray her or not. Mujahid and Qatadah said the same. Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him said regarding the verse {and what the breasts conceal}, it is He knows if you have power over her, whether you will commit adultery with her or not. As-Suddi said, and what the breasts conceal means whispers. And the Almighty said: And God judges with truth meaning He rules with justice. Al-A’mash said, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the Almighty’s saying: And God judges with truth He is able to reward good for good and bad for bad. Indeed, God is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing. This is how Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him interpreted this verse, like the Almighty’s saying: That He may recompense those who do evil for what they have done and recompense those who do good with good. And the Almighty’s saying: And those they invoke besides Him meaning idols, statues, and rivals do not judge at all meaning they do not own anything and do not rule at all. Indeed, God is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing meaning He hears the words of His creation and sees them, so He guides whomever He wills and misguides whomever He wills, and He is the just judge in all of that.

40:21: God Almighty says: Have they not traveled - these who denied your message, O Muhammad - through the land and observed what was the end of those before them - that is, of the nations who denied the prophets, peace and blessings be upon them, and what befell them of torment and humiliation, even though they were stronger than these people. And left traces on the land - that is, they left traces on the land of buildings, landmarks, and houses that these people are unable to do, as God Almighty said: And We had certainly empowered them in that in which We have not empowered you. And God Almighty said: And they tilled the land and populated it more than they had populated it - that is, despite this great strength and severe might, God seized them for their sins, which was their disbelief in His messengers. And they had no protector from God - that is, no one averted God's punishment from them, nor repelled it from them, nor protected them. Then He mentioned the reason for His seizing them and the sins that they committed and perpetrated, so God Almighty said: That is because their messengers used to come to them with clear proofs - that is, with clear evidence and conclusive proofs. But they disbelieved. That is, despite this statement and proof, they disbelieved and denied. So God seized them, meaning He destroyed them and ruined them. And there is the same for the disbelievers. He is Powerful, Severe in penalty, meaning He has great power and severe punishment. Severe in penalty, meaning His punishment is painful, severe, and hurtful. May God Almighty protect us from it.

40:23: God Almighty says, consoling His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, for the denial of those among his people who denied him, and giving him good tidings that the outcome and victory will be his in this world and the hereafter, as happened to Moses, son of Imran, peace be upon him, for God Almighty sent him with clear signs and evident evidence. That is why God the Almighty said: With Our signs and clear authority and authority is the proof and evidence to Pharaoh who was the king of the Copts in Egypt and Haman who was his minister in his kingdom and Korah who was the richest and most traded person of his time and they said, ‘A lying magician’ that is, they called him a liar, a mad magician, a deceiver, and a liar in that God had sent him. This is like the words of God the Almighty: Likewise, no messenger came to those before them except that they said, ‘A magician or a madman.’ Do they enjoin him on one another? Rather, they are a transgressing people “But when he brought them the truth from Us” that is, with the conclusive proof indicating that God the Almighty had sent him to them, they said, ‘Kill the sons of those who believed with him and keep their women alive’ This is a second command from Pharaoh to kill the males of the Children of Israel. As for the first, it was to guard against the presence of Moses, or to humiliate these people and reduce their numbers, or for the combination of both matters. As for the second matter, it was for the second reason, to insult these people, and so that they would have a bad omen about Moses, peace be upon him. For this reason, they said: “We were harmed before you came to us, and after you came to us. He said: ‘Perhaps your Lord will destroy your enemy and make you successors in the land and see how you act.’” Qatadah said: This is one matter after another. God Almighty said: And the plot of the disbelievers is only in error. That is, their plot and intention, which was to reduce the number of the Children of Israel so that they would not be victorious over them, was only lost and perishing in error. “And Pharaoh said: ‘Leave me to kill Moses, and let him call upon his Lord.’” This is a determination from Pharaoh, may God curse him, to kill Moses, peace be upon him. That is, he said to his al-Nas 114:“Leave me until I kill this man for you. ‘And let him call upon his Lord.’” That is, he did not care about him. This is the height of denial, aggression, and stubbornness. His statement, may God curse it: Indeed, I fear that he will change your religion or that corruption will appear in the land, meaning Moses. He fears. Pharaoh wanted Moses to mislead the people and change their customs and traditions. This is as the saying goes: Pharaoh became a preacher, meaning a preacher who pitied the people because of Moses, peace be upon him. Most read that he should change your religion or that corruption should appear on earth. Others read that he should change your religion or that corruption should appear on earth. Some of them read that corruption should appear on earth with the dammah. And Moses said, ‘Indeed, I have sought refuge in my Lord and your Lord from every arrogant one who does not believe in the Day of Account. That is, when he heard Pharaoh’s words, Let me kill Moses, Moses, peace be upon him, said, I seek refuge in God and in Him from his evil and the evil of his likes. That is why he said, Indeed, I have sought refuge in my Lord and your Lord, O you who are being addressed, from every arrogant one, that is, a criminal who turns away from the truth, who does not believe in the Day of Account. That is why it is mentioned in the hadith on the authority of Abu Musa, may God be pleased with him, that whenever the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, feared a people, he would say, O God, we seek refuge in You from their evils and ward off their evil through You.
