40:28: It is well known that this believing man was a Copt from the family of Pharaoh. Al-Suddi said: He was Pharaoh's cousin and it is said that he was the one who escaped with Moses, peace be upon him. Ibn Jarir chose this and rejected the statement of those who said that he was an Israelite because Pharaoh was moved by his words and listened to him and refrained from killing Moses, peace be upon him. If he had been an Israelite, he would have been likely to be punished quickly because he was from them. Ibn Jurayj said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, that no one from the family of Pharaoh believed except this man and Pharaoh's wife and the one who said: O Moses, the leaders are conspiring to kill you. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. This man concealed his faith from his Coptic people and it did not appear until this day when Pharaoh said, Let me kill Moses. So the wrath of God Almighty seized the man. The best jihad is a word of justice in front of a tyrannical ruler, as proven by this hadith. There is nothing greater than this word in front of Pharaoh, which is his saying: Would you kill a man because he says, ‘My Lord is God,’ except for what Al-Bukhari narrated in his Sahih where he said: Ali bin Abdullah narrated to us, Al-Walid bin Muslim narrated to us, Al-Awza’i narrated to us, Yahya bin Abi Katheer narrated to me, Muhammad bin Ibrahim Al-Taymi narrated to me, Urwah bin Az-Zubayr narrated to me, may God be pleased with them both, he said: I said to Abdullah bin Amr bin Al-Aas, may God be pleased with them both, tell me the worst thing the polytheists did to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: While the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was praying in the courtyard of the Kaaba, Uqbah bin Abi Mu’ayt came and seized the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, by the shoulder, twisted his garment around his neck, and choked him violently. Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, came and seized his shoulder and pushed him away from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, then he said: Would you kill a man because he says, ‘My Lord is God,’ when he has come to you with clear proofs from your Lord? Al-Bukhari transmitted it exclusively from the hadith of Al-Awza’i. He said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq followed him on the authority of Yahya ibn Urwah on the authority of his father. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Harun ibn Ishaq Al-Hamadani told us: Abdah told us on the authority of Hisham, meaning Ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Amr ibn Al-As may God be pleased with him that he was asked: What is the most severe thing you saw the Quraysh do to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him)? He said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) passed by them one day and they said to him: Are you forbidding us to worship what our fathers worshipped? He said: I am that one. So they went to him and grabbed the hem of his garment. I saw Abu Bakr may God be pleased with him embracing him from behind, shouting at the top of his voice, his eyes watering, and he was saying: O my people, would you kill a man because he says, ‘My Lord is God,’ while he has come to you with clear proofs from your Lord? until he finished the entire verse. This is how it was narrated by Al-Nasa’i from the hadith of Abdah, so he included it in the Musnad of Amr ibn Al-Aas may God be pleased with him. The Almighty’s statement: And he has come to you with clear proofs from your Lord means how could you kill a man because he says, My Lord is God, while he has provided you with proof of the truth that he has brought to you? Then he addressed them and said: “And if he is a liar, then upon him is his lie. But if he is truthful, some of what he promises you will befall you.” Meaning, if the truth of what he brought you is not clear to you, then it is wise, sound judgment, and prudent to leave him alone and not harm him. If he is a liar, then God, the Most High, will punish him for his lie in this world and the next. And if he is truthful and you have harmed him, then some of what he promises you will befall you. He threatens you, if you disobey him, with punishment in this world and the next. So it is possible for you that he is truthful, so based on this, you should not interfere with him. Rather, leave him and his people so that they may call them and follow him. Thus, God the Almighty told about Moses, peace be upon him, that he asked Pharaoh and his people for a truce in His saying: “And We had certainly tried before them the people of Pharaoh, and there came to them a noble messenger, saying, ‘Give me the servants of God. Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger, and do not exalt yourselves over God. Indeed, I have come to you with clear authority. And I have sought refuge in my Lord and your Lord, that you should stone me. And if you do not believe in me, then leave me alone.’” Thus, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to the Quraysh that they should leave him calling to God the Almighty, the servants of God, and not harm him, and maintain the kinship between him and them by not harming him. God the Almighty said: Say, ‘I do not ask of you any reward for this except love for the sake of kinship.’ That is, do not harm me regarding the kinship between me and you, so do not harm me and leave me alone with the people. And based on this, the truce took place on the day of Hudaybiyyah, and it was a clear victory. And the Almighty said: Indeed, God does not guide one who is a transgressor and a liar, meaning if this one who claims that God the Almighty sent him to you was a liar, as you claim, then he would have been…” His command is clear and apparent to everyone in his words and actions, so it was in the utmost disagreement and confusion. We see his command as sound and his approach as upright. If he had been one of the extravagant liars, God would not have guided him and directed him to what you see of the order of his command and action. Then the believer said, warning his people of the removal of God’s blessing from them and the descent of God’s punishment upon them: O my people, yours is the kingdom this Day, dominant in the land. That is, God has bestowed upon you this kingdom and dominance in the land with the effective word and broad prestige, so take care of this blessing by thanking God Almighty and believing in His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and beware of God’s punishment if you lie about His Messenger. Then who will protect us from the punishment of God if it comes to us? That is, these soldiers and these armies will not avail you and will not repel from us anything of God’s punishment if He intends us harm. Pharaoh said to his people, responding to what this righteous, pious, and well-guided man, who was more deserving of the kingdom than Pharaoh, had suggested: I only show you what I see. That is, I do not say to you and advise you except what I see for myself. Pharaoh lied, for he Moses, peace be upon him, was convinced of the truthfulness of the message he brought: He said, ‘Indeed, you know that none has sent down these except the Lord of the heavens and the earth as insights.’ And God Almighty said: And they denied them, though their souls were convinced thereof, out of injustice and arrogance. So his saying, I show you only what I see, was a lie and a fabrication in it, and he betrayed God Almighty, His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his subjects, for he deceived them and did not advise them. He also lied in that, even though his people obeyed him and followed him. God Almighty said: So they followed the command of Pharaoh, and Pharaoh’s command was not right. And He, the Most High, said: And Pharaoh led his people astray and did not guide them. If he had been an Israelite, he would have been likely to be punished quickly because he was from them. Ibn Jurayj said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, that no one from the family of Pharaoh believed except this man and Pharaoh's wife and the one who said: O Moses, the leaders are conspiring to kill you. 40:30: This is report from God the Almighty about this righteous man, the believer of the family of Pharaoh, that he warned his people of the punishment of God the Almighty in this world and the hereafter, so he said: O my people, indeed I fear for you a Day like that of the Confederates, meaning those who denied the messengers of God in ancient times, such as the people of Noah, Aad, and Thamud, and those who came after them from the nations of disbelief, how the punishment of God befell them, and no one repelled it from them, nor did anyone repel it from them. And God does not intend injustice to His servants, meaning God the Almighty destroyed them because of their sins, their denial of His messengers, and their disobedience to His command, so He executed His decree upon them. Then he said: And O my people, indeed I fear for you the Day of Calling, meaning the Day of Resurrection, and it was called that. Some of them said that when it came in the hadith of the trumpet that when the earth is shaken and splits from one region to another and shudders and shakes, and people see that, they run away, calling out to one another. Others, including Ad-Dahhak, said: Rather, that is when their jinn are brought, people run away from them, and the angels meet them and return them to the station of The Gathering, which is the Almighty’s saying: And the King is over its corners, and His saying: “O company of jinn and mankind, if you are able to pass beyond the regions of the heavens and the earth, then pass. You will not pass except by authority.” It has been narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, Al-Hasan and Ad-Dahhak that they read The Day of Calling with a shaddah on the dal from the call of a camel when it strays and goes. It was said that because the scale has an angel who, if he weighs the deeds of the servant and they are heavier, calls out at the top of his voice, Indeed, so-and-so, son of so-and-so, has been made happy, a happiness after which he will never be miserable. And if his deeds are light, he calls out, Indeed, so-and-so, son of so-and-so, has been made miserable. Qatada said: Every people calls out their deeds. The people of Paradise call out to the people of Paradise and the people of Hell call out to the people of Hell. It was said that it was called that because the people of Paradise call out to the people of Hell, “Indeed, we have found what our Lord promised us to be true. Have you found what your Lord promised to be true?” They said, "Yes. And the people of Hell will call out to the people of Paradise, Pour upon us some water or from whatever God has provided you. They will say, Indeed, God has forbidden them both to the disbelievers." And the call of the people of A'raf to the people of Paradise and the people of Hell, as mentioned in Surat Al-A'raf. Al-Baghawi and others chose that it was named thus for the sum of that, and it is a good and fine statement, and God knows best. And the statement of God, the Most High: "The Day you turn back, fleeing," meaning going and fleeing. "No, there is no burden. To your Lord, that Day, is the final settlement." For this reason, God, the Most High, said: "You will have no protector from God," meaning there is no protector to prevent you from God's wrath and punishment. "And he whom God sends astray, for him there is no guide," meaning he whom God sends astray, for him there is no guide other than Him. And the statement of God, the Most High: "And indeed, Joseph came to you before with clear proofs," meaning the people of Egypt, and God sent among them a messenger before Moses, peace be upon him, and he is Joseph, peace be upon him. He was the noble one of the people of Egypt, and he was a messenger calling his nation to God, the Most High, with justice, but they did not obey him in that obedience except for the sake of ministry and worldly prestige. For this reason, God, the Most High, said: "So what You remained in doubt about what he brought you until, when he died, you said, God will never send after him a messenger. That is, you despaired and said, hoping, God will never send after him a messenger. This was due to their disbelief and denial. Thus does God send astray he who is a transgressor, full of doubt. That is, this is the state of one whom God sends astray due to his transgression in his actions and the doubt in his heart. Then the Almighty said, Those who dispute concerning the verses of God without any authority that has come to them. That is, those who reject the truth with falsehood and dispute with arguments without any proof or argument from God Almighty. God Almighty hates that with the utmost hatred. For this reason, the Almighty said, It is most hateful in the sight of God and to those who believe. That is, the believers also hate those who have this characteristic. For whoever has this characteristic, God seals his heart so that he does not know what is right nor denounce what is wrong. For this reason, the Almighty said, Thus does God seal the heart of every arrogant person. That is, he who follows the truth a tyrant. Abu Imran al-Joni and Qatada said: The sign of tyrants is killing without right. And God Almighty knows best.

And if his deeds are light, he calls out, Indeed, so-and-so, son of so-and-so, has been made miserable. Qatada said: Every people calls out their deeds. The people of Paradise call out to the people of Paradise and the people of Hell call out to the people of Hell. It was said that it was called that because the people of Paradise call out to the people of Hell, “Indeed, we have found what our Lord promised us to be true. Have you found what your Lord promised to be true?” They said, "Yes. And the people of Hell will call out to the people of Paradise, Pour upon us some water or from whatever God has provided you. They will say, Indeed, God has forbidden them both to the disbelievers." And the call of the people of A'raf to the people of Paradise and the people of Hell, as mentioned in Surat Al-A'raf. Al-Baghawi and others chose that it was named thus for the sum of that, and it is a good and fine statement, and God knows best. For this reason, God, the Most High, said: "You will have no protector from God," meaning there is no protector to prevent you from God's wrath and punishment. "And he whom God sends astray, for him there is no guide," meaning he whom God sends astray, for him there is no guide other than Him. And the statement of God, the Most High: "And indeed, Joseph came to you before with clear proofs," meaning the people of Egypt, and God sent among them a messenger before Moses, peace be upon him, and he is Joseph, peace be upon him. He was the noble one of the people of Egypt, and he was a messenger calling his nation to God, the Most High, with justice, but they did not obey him in that obedience except for the sake of ministry and worldly prestige. For this reason, God, the Most High, said: "So what You remained in doubt about what he brought you until, when he died, you said, God will never send after him a messenger. That is, you despaired and said, hoping, God will never send after him a messenger. This was due to their disbelief and denial. Thus does God send astray he who is a transgressor, full of doubt. That is, this is the state of one whom God sends astray due to his transgression in his actions and the doubt in his heart. Then the Almighty said, Those who dispute concerning the verses of God without any authority that has come to them. That is, those who reject the truth with falsehood and dispute with arguments without any proof or argument from God Almighty. God Almighty hates that with the utmost hatred. For this reason, the Almighty said, It is most hateful in the sight of God and to those who believe. That is, the believers also hate those who have this characteristic. For whoever has this characteristic, God seals his heart so that he does not know what is right nor denounce what is wrong. For this reason, the Almighty said, Thus does God seal the heart of every arrogant person. That is, he who follows the truth a tyrant. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ikrimah and it was narrated on the authority of Al-Sha’bi that they both said: They said: A person is not a tyrant until he kills two people. Abu Imran al-Joni and Qatada said: The sign of tyrants is killing without right. And God Almighty knows best.

It was made of bricks beaten from baked clay, as God the Almighty said: Then kindle for me a fire, O Haman, over the clay and make for me a tower. For this reason, Ibrahim al-Nakha’i said, They hated to build with bricks and to put them in their graves. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. And His statement, Perhaps I may reach the causes * the causes of the heavens, etc. Sa’id ibn Jubayr and Abu Salih said, The gates of the heavens, and it was said, The paths of the heavens. “Then I may look at the God of Moses, and indeed, I think he is a liar.” This is from his disbelief and rebellion, that he lied to Moses, peace be upon him, that God the Almighty sent him to him. God the Almighty said: And thus the evil of his work was made fair-seeming to Pharaoh, and he was averted from the way. That is, by this action of his, by which he wanted to make the subjects believe that he was doing something to reach the denial of Moses, peace be upon him. For this reason, God the Almighty said: And the plot of Pharaoh was only in vain. Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said: It means only in loss.

40:38: The believer says to his people who rebelled and transgressed and preferred the life of this world and forgot the Almighty, the Most High, and says to them: O my people, follow me, and I will guide you to the path of right conduct. Not as Pharaoh lied when he said: I do not guide you except to the path of right conduct. Then he made them renounce the life of this world, which they preferred over the other, and prevented them from believing in the Messenger of God, Moses, peace be upon him, and said: O my people, this worldly life is only a temporary enjoyment, meaning it is brief, fleeting, and soon it will go away and vanish. And indeed, the Hereafter is the home of permanence, meaning the home that does not perish, nor move from it, nor depart from it to another, but rather it is either bliss or Hellfire. For this reason, the Most High said: Whoever does an evil will not be recompensed except with the like thereof, meaning one like it. And whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while he is a believer - those will enter Paradise and will be provided for therein without account, meaning it will not be measured by a reward, but God Almighty will reward them with a great reward that will never end or run out. And God Almighty is the Grantor of success in what is right.

40:41: The believer says to them: What is wrong with me that I call you to salvation, which is the worship of God alone, with no partner, and the belief in His Messenger whom God sent? “And you invite me to the Fire. You invite me to disbelieve in God and associate with Him that of which I have no knowledge.” That is, out of ignorance and without proof. And I invite you to the Exalted in Might, the Forgiving. That is, He, in His might and pride, forgives the sin of whoever repents to Him. Indeed, you invite me to it. He says, Truly? Al-Suddi and Ibn Jarir said that the meaning of his saying, Indeed, you invite me to it is truly. Ad-Dahhak said, No crime, meaning, no lie. Ali ibn Abi Talha said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, No crime, meaning, Yes, that to which you call me of idols and rivals, ‘He has no call in this world or in the Hereafter.’ Mujahid said, The idol has nothing. Qatadah said, It means that the idol neither benefits nor harms. As-Suddi said, It does not answer its caller, neither in this world nor in the Hereafter. This is like the statement of God, the Most High, “And who is more astray than he who calls upon others besides God, who will not respond to him until the Day of Resurrection, and they, of their call, are unaware? And when the people are gathered together, they will be enemies to them and will be disbelievers in their worship.” If you call upon them, they will not hear your call, and if they heard, they would not respond to you. And His statement, And that our return is to God, meaning in the Hereafter, so He will reward each one according to his deeds. For this reason, He said, And that the transgressors are the companions of the Fire, meaning, they will abide therein forever because of their transgression, which is their associating partners with God, the Almighty. Then you will remember what I say to you, meaning, you will know the truth of what I have commanded you to do and what I have forbidden you from doing. I advised you and made it clear to you, and you remember it and regret it when regret is of no use. And I entrust my affair to God, meaning I put my trust in God and seek His help, and I boycott you and keep you away. Indeed, God is Seeing of His servants, meaning He is Seeing of them, the Most High and Most Holy. He guides whomever deserves guidance and misguides whomever deserves misguidance. He has the conclusive argument, perfect wisdom, and effective power. And the saying of God, the Most High: So God saved him from the evil of their plotting meaning in this world and the Hereafter. As for this world, God saved him with Moses, peace be upon him, and as for the Hereafter, he will be in Paradise. And the people of Pharaoh were encompassed by an evil punishment meaning drowning in the sea and then being transferred from it to Hell. Their souls will be exposed to the Fire morning and evening until the Day of Resurrection. So when the Day of Resurrection comes, their souls and bodies will be gathered together in the Fire. For this reason, He said: And on the Day the Hour appears, admit Pharaoh’s people into the severest punishment meaning the most painful and the greatest punishment. This verse is a major basis for the Sunnis’ evidence for the torment of the intermediate realm in the graves, and it is the saying of God, the Most High: The Fire they will be exposed to morning and evening. But here is a question, which is that there is no doubt that this verse is Meccan, and they used it as evidence for the torment of the grave in the Barzakh. Imam Ahmad said: Hashim told us, he is Ibn Al-Qasim Abu Al-Nadr, Ishaq Ibn Saeed, he is Ibn Amr Ibn Saeed Ibn Al-As, Saeed told us, meaning his father, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, that a Jewish woman used to serve her, and whenever Aisha, may God be pleased with her, did anything good for her, the Jewish woman would say to her, May God protect you from the torment of the grave. She, may God be pleased with her, said: Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to me, and I said: O Messenger of God, is there a torment in the grave before the Day of Resurrection? He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: No, who claims that? This Jewess said, I will not do her any good deed except that she will say, ‘May God protect you from the punishment of the grave.’ The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, “The Jews lied, and they are the biggest liar to God. There is no punishment before the Day of Resurrection.” Then he stayed for as long as God willed him to stay. Then one day he came out at noon, covered with his garment, his eyes red, and he was calling out at the top of his voice, “The grave is like pieces of a dark night. O people, if you knew what I know, you would weep much and laugh little. O people, seek refuge in God from the punishment of the grave, for the punishment of the grave is true.” This is a sound chain of transmission according to the criteria of Bukhari and Muslim, but they did not include it. Ahmad narrated that Yazid told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Aisha may God be pleased with her, who said, “A Jewish woman asked her for something, and she gave it to her. She said to her, ‘May God protect you from the punishment of the grave.’ Aisha may God be pleased with her did not approve of that, but when she saw the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), she said to him, and he (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, ‘No.’ Aisha may God be pleased with her said, “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) then said to us after that, ‘It has been revealed to me that you will be tested in your graves.’” This also according to their criteria. It is said: What is the connection between this and the fact that the verse was revealed in Mecca and that it contains evidence of the torment of the intermediate realm? The answer is that the verse indicates that the souls are exposed to the Fire morning and evening in the intermediate realm. It does not indicate that their pain is connected to their bodies in the graves, as this might be specific to the soul. As for the occurrence of this in the intermediate realm for the body and its pain because of it, this is only indicated by the Sunnah in the acceptable hadiths mentioned below. It may be said that this verse only indicates the torment of the disbelievers in the intermediate realm, and this does not necessarily mean that the believer will be tormented in his grave for a sin. Evidence of this is what Imam Ahmad narrated: Uthman bin Umar narrated to us, Yunus narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered upon her and there was a Jewish woman with her, and she was saying, Do you know that you will be tested in your graves? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was startled and said, Only the Jews will be tested. Aisha, may God be pleased with her, said, “We stayed for a few nights, then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, “Behold, you will be tested in the graves.” Aisha, may God be pleased with her, said, “Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would seek refuge from the torment of the grave.” Muslim narrated it in this way, on the authority of Harun bin Saeed and Harmalah, both of them on the authority of Ibn Wahb, on the authority of Yunus bin Yazid Al-Ayli, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on his authority. It may be said that this verse indicates the torment of the souls in the intermediate realm, but it does not necessarily mean that it is connected to the bodies in their graves. So when the revelation was sent to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) concerning that in particular, he sought refuge from it, and God knows best. Al-Bukhari narrated from the hadeeth of Shu’bah, from Ash’ath ibn Abi Ash-Sha’tha’, from his father, from Masruq, from Aisha may God be pleased with her, that a Jewish woman entered upon her and said, We seek refuge in God from the torment of the grave. Aisha may God be pleased with her asked the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) about the torment of the grave, and he (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, Yes, the torment of the grave is true. Aisha may God be pleased with her said, “I never saw the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) pray a prayer after that without seeking refuge from the torment of the grave.” This indicates that he, may God bless him and grant him peace, hastened to believe the Jewish report and decided upon it. In the previous report, he denied it until the revelation came to him, so perhaps they are two issues, and God Almighty knows best. The hadiths about the torment of the grave are very numerous. Qatada said about the Almighty’s statement: morning and evening morning and evening as long as the world remains, it will be said to them, O family of Pharaoh, these are your dwellings, as a rebuke, punishment, and humiliation for them. Ibn Zayd said, They are in it today, being taken to and from until the Hour comes. He said: Ibn Abi Hatim told us, Abu Saeed told us, Al-Maharbi told us, Laith told us, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Tharwan, on the authority of Hudhayl, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, may God be pleased with him, who said: The souls of the martyrs are in the bodies of green birds that roam with them in Paradise wherever they wish. The souls of the children of the believers are in the bodies of sparrows that roam in Paradise wherever they wish and take refuge in lamps suspended from the Throne. The souls of the family of Pharaoh are in the bodies of black birds that go to Hell in the morning and in the evening, and that is its width. Al-Thawri narrated it on the authority of Abu Qais on the authority of Hudhayl bin Shurahbil from his words about the souls of the family of Pharaoh, and Al-Suddi said the same. This is like the statement of God, the Most High, “And who is more astray than he who calls upon others besides God, who will not respond to him until the Day of Resurrection, and they, of their call, are unaware? And when the people are gathered together, they will be enemies to them and will be disbelievers in their worship.” If you call upon them, they will not hear your call, and if they heard, they would not respond to you. And His statement, And that our return is to God, meaning in the Hereafter, so He will reward each one according to his deeds. For this reason, He said, And that the transgressors are the companions of the Fire, meaning, they will abide therein forever because of their transgression, which is their associating partners with God, the Almighty. Then you will remember what I say to you, meaning, you will know the truth of what I have commanded you to do and what I have forbidden you from doing. I advised you and made it clear to you, and you remember it and regret it when regret is of no use. And I entrust my affair to God, meaning I put my trust in God and seek His help, and I boycott you and keep you away. Indeed, God is Seeing of His servants, meaning He is Seeing of them, the Most High and Most Holy. He guides whomever deserves guidance and misguides whomever deserves misguidance. He has the conclusive argument, perfect wisdom, and effective power. And the saying of God, the Most High: So God saved him from the evil of their plotting meaning in this world and the Hereafter. As for this world, God saved him with Moses, peace be upon him, and as for the Hereafter, he will be in Paradise. And the people of Pharaoh were encompassed by an evil punishment meaning drowning in the sea and then being transferred from it to Hell. Their souls will be exposed to the Fire morning and evening until the Day of Resurrection. So when the Day of Resurrection comes, their souls and bodies will be gathered together in the Fire. For this reason, He said: And on the Day the Hour appears, admit Pharaoh’s people into the severest punishment meaning the most painful and the greatest punishment. He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: No, who claims that? This Jewess said, I will not do her any good deed except that she will say, ‘May God protect you from the punishment of the grave.’ The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, “The Jews lied, and they are the biggest liar to God. There is no punishment before the Day of Resurrection.” Then he stayed for as long as God willed him to stay. Then one day he came out at noon, covered with his garment, his eyes red, and he was calling out at the top of his voice, “The grave is like pieces of a dark night. O people, if you knew what I know, you would weep much and laugh little. O people, seek refuge in God from the punishment of the grave, for the punishment of the grave is true.” This is a sound chain of transmission according to the criteria of Bukhari and Muslim, but they did not include it. Ibn Zayd said, They are in it today, being taken to and from until the Hour comes. He said: Ibn Abi Hatim told us, Abu Saeed told us, Al-Maharbi told us, Laith told us, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Tharwan, on the authority of Hudhayl, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, may God be pleased with him, who said: The souls of the martyrs are in the bodies of green birds that roam with them in Paradise wherever they wish. The souls of the children of the believers are in the bodies of sparrows that roam in Paradise wherever they wish and take refuge in lamps suspended from the Throne. The souls of the family of Pharaoh are in the bodies of black birds that go to Hell in the morning and in the evening, and that is its width. We said: O Messenger of God, what is God’s reward for the disbeliever? He said: If he has maintained family ties or given charity or done a good deed, God Almighty will reward him with wealth, children, health, and the like. We said: So what… His reward in the Hereafter? He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: A punishment less severe than this punishment. Then he recited: Enter the people of Pharaoh into the severest punishment. Al-Bazzar narrated it in his Musnad on the authority of Zayd ibn Akram, then he said: We do not know of any other chain of narration for it other than this. Ibn Jarir said: Abdul-Karim ibn Abi ‘Umayr told us: Hammad ibn Muhammad al-Fazari al-Balkhi told us: I heard al-Awza’i when a man asked him: May God have mercy on you. He said: Did you realise that? He said: Yes. He said: Those birds have in their crops the souls of Pharaoh’s family. They are shown to the Fire morning and evening, and they return to their nests with their feathers burned and turned black. Then white feathers grow on them at night and the black ones scatter. Then they go to the Fire morning and evening, and then they return to their nests. That is their way in this world. When the Day of Resurrection comes, God the Most High will say: Enter the family of Pharaoh into the severest punishment. He said: And they used to say that they were six hundred thousand fighters. Imam Ahmad said: Ishaq told us, Malik told us, from Nafi’, from Ibn ‘Umar, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When one of you dies, his seat is shown to him morning and evening. If he is from the people of Paradise, then he is from the people of Paradise, and if he is from the people of Hell, then he is from the people of Hell. Then it is said: This is your seat until God the Almighty raises you to it on the Day of Resurrection.” They narrated it in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Malik with it.

40:47: God Almighty tells us about the people of Hell arguing and quarreling in Hell, and Pharaoh and his people among them. The weak ones, who are the followers, will say to those who were arrogant, who are the leaders, masters, and notables: Indeed, we were your followers, meaning we obeyed you in what you called us to in this world of disbelief and misguidance. So can you relieve us of a portion of the Fire? meaning a share that you will bear on our behalf? “Those who were arrogant will say: “Indeed, we are all in it.” That is, we will not bear anything on your behalf. What we have and what we have carried of torment and punishment is sufficient for us. Indeed, God has judged between His servants. That is, He has divided the torment among us according to what each of us deserves, as God Almighty said: He said, ‘To each is weakness, but you do not know.’ “And those in the Fire will say to the keepers of Hell: ‘Call upon your Lord to lighten for us a day of the torment.’” When they knew that God Almighty does not respond to them or listen to their supplication, but rather He said: Be gone into it, despised and disgraced, and do not speak. They asked the keepers, who are like jailers for the people of Hell. To call upon God for them to lighten the punishment for the disbelievers even for one day. The keepers said to them, responding, Did not your messengers come to you with clear proofs? That is, did the arguments not come to you in this world through the tongues of the messengers? They said, Yes. They said, Then call upon God. That is, you are for yourselves, for we will not call upon you, nor will we listen to you, nor do we wish to save you, and we are innocent of you. Then we inform you that whether you call upon God or not, your punishment will not be answered and your punishment will not be lightened. For this reason they said, And the supplication of the disbelievers is only in error. That is, it is in error and will not be accepted or answered.

40:57: The Almighty says, pointing out that He will restore creation on the Day of Resurrection and that this is easy and simple for Him, that He created the heavens and the earth, and their creation is greater than the creation of people, beginning and repeating. So whoever is able to do that is even more able to do what is less than it, as the Almighty says: Do they not see that God, who created the heavens and the earth and was not weary in their creation, is able to give life to the dead? Yes, He is over all things competent. And He says here: The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of people, but most people do not know. For this reason, they do not ponder this argument or consider it, just as many of the Arabs admitted that God Almighty created the heavens and the earth and denied the Resurrection out of estrangement, disbelief, and stubbornness. They admitted what was more appropriate than what they denied. Then the Almighty says: “And not equal are the blind and the seeing, and those who believe and do righteous deeds and the evildoer. Little do you remember.” That is, just as the blind who does not see anything are not equal to the seeing who sees what his sight reaches, but rather there is a great difference between them, likewise the righteous believers are not equal to the disbelievers. The wicked You remember little meaning how little many people remember. Then God Almighty said: The Hour is coming meaning it will happen and will occur there is no doubt about it, but most of the people do not believe meaning they do not believe in it, rather they deny its existence. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abdul Hakam told us, Ashab told us, Malik told us, on the authority of an old sheikh from the people of Yemen who came from there, he said: I heard that when the Hour draws near, the calamities will intensify for the people and the heat of the sun will become intense. And God knows best.

40:61: The Almighty says, thanking His creation for what He has given them of the night in which they rest and rest from the movements of their hesitation in their livelihoods during the day, and He has made the day visible, that is, luminous, so that they can travel, cross countries, and be able to do industry. Indeed, God is full of bounty to mankind, but most people do not give thanks. That is, they do not give thanks for the blessings of God upon them. Then the Almighty said: “That is God, your Lord, the Creator of all things. There is no god except Him.” That is, the One who did these things is God, the One, the Creator of things, other than whom there is no god and no lord. So how are you deluded? That is, how can you worship idols that do not create anything, but are created and carved. And the Almighty said: Thus are those who used to deny the signs of God deluded. That is, just as those who were led astray by worshipping other than God were deluded by those who came before them, so they worshipped other than Him without proof or evidence, but rather out of mere ignorance and desire. They denied the proofs and signs of God and His saying: God is He who has made the earth a resting place for you meaning He made it a stable place for you, a comfortable place to live on, move around in, and walk in its paths, and He anchored it with mountains so that it would not shake with you. And the sky is a structure meaning a preserved roof for the world. And He shaped you and perfected your shapes meaning He created you in the best forms and gave you the most perfect forms in the best stature. And provided for you of the good things meaning of the food and drink in this world. So He mentioned that He is the Creator of the home, the inhabitants, and the provisions, for He is the Creator and Provider, as God the Almighty said in Surat al-Baqarah 2:“O mankind, worship your Lord, who created you and those before you that you may become righteous. * Who made the earth a resting place for you and the sky a canopy and sent down water from the sky and brought forth thereby fruits as provision for you. So do not attribute to God equals while you know.” And the Almighty said here after creating these things: Such is God, your Lord, so blessed is God, Lord of the worlds. That is, He is exalted, sanctified, and transcendent, the Lord of all the worlds. Then the Almighty said: He is the Ever-Living, there is no god except Him. That is, He is the Ever-Living, eternally and forever. He has always been and will always be. He is the First and the Last, the Evident and the Hidden. There is no god except Him. That is, He has no equal or equal. So call upon Him, making your religion sincere to Him. That is, believing in His Oneness and affirming that there is no god except Him. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds. Ibn Jarir said: A group of scholars used to order whoever says There is no god except God to follow it with Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds, acting on this verse. Then it was narrated on the authority of Muhammad bin Ali bin Al-Hasan bin Shaqiq, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Hussein bin Waqid, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Whoever says There is no god but God should say after it Praise be to God, Lord of the Worlds. This is the saying of the Most High: “So call upon Him, making your religion sincere to Him. Praise be to God, Lord of the Worlds.” Abu Usamah and others said on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, who said: When you recite So call upon God, making your religion sincere to Him, then say There is no god but God and say after it Praise be to God, Lord of the Worlds. Then he recited: “So call upon Him, making your religion sincere to Him. Praise be to God, Lord of the Worlds.” Imam Ahmad said: Ibn Numayr told us, Hisham - meaning Ibn Urwah Ibn Az-Zubayr - told us, on the authority of Abu Az-Zubayr Muhammad Ibn Muslim Ibn Badr Al-Makki, who said: Abdullah Ibn Az-Zubayr used to say after every prayer when he finished the salutation: “There is no god but God alone, with no partner. His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He is over all things omnipotent. There is no power nor strength save with God. There is no god but God, and we do not worship except Him. His is the blessing and His is the bounty and His is the best praise. There is no god but God, making religion sincere to Him, even though the disbelievers hate it.” He said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to say them after every prayer. Muslim, Abu Dawud, and An-Nasa’i narrated it through various chains of narration on the authority of Hisham Ibn Urwah, Hajjaj Ibn Abi Uthman, and Musa Ibn Uqbah, all three of them, on the authority of Abu Az-Zubayr, on the authority of Abdullah Ibn Az-Zubayr, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to say after every prayer: There is no god but God alone, with no partner. And he mentioned the rest of it.

40:66: The Blessed and Exalted says: Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists that God Almighty forbids the worship of anyone other than Him, from idols, rivals, and statues. The Blessed and Exalted has made it clear that no one deserves worship other than Him in His statement, may His Majesty be glorified: “It is He who created you from dust, then from a sperm-drop, then from a clinging clot. Then He brings you forth as a child, then that you may reach your full strength, then that you may be old men.” That is, He is the One who turns you through all these stages alone, with no partner for Him, and that is by His command, management, and decree. And among you is he who dies before, that is, before he comes into existence and comes out into this world. Rather, his mother miscarries him as a miscarriage. And among them is he who dies young, young, or old before old age, as the Almighty says: “That We may make clear to you. And We cause whom We will to remain in the wombs for a specified term.” And the Almighty said here: And that you may reach a specified term and that you may understand. Ibn Jurayj said: You remember the resurrection. Then the Almighty said: It is He who gives life. And He causes death” meaning He is the only One who can do that. No one else is able to do that. So when He decrees a matter, He only says to it, ‘Be,’ and it is. Meaning, He does not oppose or prevent it. Rather, whatever He wills will inevitably be.

And He, the Majestic and Sublime, says: When the shackles are around their necks and the chains meaning connected to the shackles by the hands of the guardians, dragging them on their faces, sometimes to the scalding water and sometimes to Hell. For this reason, God Almighty says: They will be dragged * into the scalding water, then in the Fire they will be blazing. As God Almighty says: “This is Hell which the criminals deny. They will circulate between it and scalding water.” And God Almighty says after mentioning their eating of Zaqqum and drinking the scalding water: “And the companions of the left - what about the companions of the left? * In scorching wind and scalding water * And in the shade of scalding water * Neither cool nor pleasant. * Indeed, they were before that.” In luxury * And they persisted in the great oath * And they used to say, When we have died and become dust and bones, will we indeed be resurrected * Or our forefathers of old? * Say, “Indeed, the first and the last * Will be gathered together for a known time on a known day. * Then indeed, you, O astray deniers * Will eat from the tree of Zaqqum * And fill your bellies therewith * And drink thereon of scalding water * And drink as boiling water would drink. This is their lodging on the Day of Judgment.” And the Almighty said: “Indeed, the tree of Zaqqum * Is the food of the sinner * Like molten brass, boiling within bellies * Like the boiling of scalding water. Seize him and drag him up to the midst of Hellfire * Then pour over his head from the punishment of scalding water. Taste. Indeed, you are the Exalted in Might, the Generous. * Indeed, this is what you were in doubt about.” That is, this is said to them in a way of rebuke, rebuke, belittling, disparaging, mocking, and ridiculing them. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali ibn al-Husayn told us, Ahmad ibn Mani’ told us, Mansur ibn Ammar told us, Bashir ibn Talhah al-Khuzami told us, on the authority of Khalid ibn Durak, on the authority of Ya’la Ibn Munabbih traced the hadith back to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “God Almighty will create a black, dark cloud for the people of Hell, and it will be said, ‘O people of Hell, what do you seek?’ They will be reminded of the clouds of this world, saying, “We ask for a cool drink,” but it will rain down shackles that will add to their shackles, chains that will add to their chains, and embers that will ignite the Fire upon them. This is a strange hadith. And the words of God, the Most High: Then it will be said to them, ‘Where are those you used to associate with God?’ That is, it will be said to them, Where are the idols you used to worship other than God? Will they aid you today? “They will say, ‘They have gone astray from us.’” That is, they have gone away and did not benefit us. Rather, we did not call upon anything before. That is, they denied their worship, as God, the Most High, said: Then their only trial was that they said, ‘By God, our Lord, we were not polytheists.’ That is, God, the Most High, said: Thus does God mislead the disbelievers. And His words: That is because you used to exult upon the earth without right and because you used to be insolent. That is, the angels will say to them, “This that you are in is a reward for your unjust exultation in this world, your exultation, your polytheism, and your arrogance. “Enter the gates of Hell to abide therein. Wretched is the abode of the arrogant.” What an evil home and resting place, in which there is humiliation and severe punishment for those who are arrogant about the signs of God and following His proofs and arguments. And God knows best.

40:77: God Almighty says, commanding His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to be patient with the denial of those among his people who denied him, for God Almighty will fulfill for you what He promised you of victory and triumph over your people and will make the outcome for you and for those who follow you in this world and the hereafter. Either We show you some of what We promise them, meaning in this world, and that is how it happened, for God Almighty comforted their eyes with their leaders and great ones who were destroyed on the day of Badr, then God opened Mecca and the rest of the Arabian Peninsula for him during his life, may God bless him and grant him peace. And the Almighty says: Or We take you in death, then to Us they will be returned, meaning We will make them taste the severe punishment in the hereafter. Then God Almighty says, consoling him: And We have certainly sent messengers before you, among them are those We have told you about, as God Almighty said in Surat An-Nisa, the same, meaning among them are those We have revealed to you their report and stories with their people, how they denied them, then the messengers had the outcome and victory. And among them are those We have not told you about, and they are many times more than those mentioned, as was previously pointed out in Surat An-Nisa. Women, praise and thanks be to God. And the Almighty said: And it was not for a messenger to bring a sign except by permission of God meaning, it was not for any of the messengers to bring anything extraordinary to his people unless God gave him permission to do so, which would indicate the truthfulness of what he brought them. So when the command of God comes which is His punishment and chastisement surrounding the deniers, it will be decided with truth so the believers will be saved and the disbelievers will be destroyed. For this reason, the Almighty said: And there the falsifiers will lose.

40:79: God Almighty says, thanking His servants for the livestock He created for them, namely camels, cows, and sheep. Some of them they ride and some they eat. Camels are ridden, eaten, milked, and heavy loads are carried on them during journeys and on trips to distant lands and vast regions. Cows are eaten, their milk is drunk, and the land is plowed. Sheep are eaten, their milk is drunk, and their wool, hair, and fur are sheared to make furniture, clothing, and luggage, as explained and explained in places mentioned previously in Surat Al-An’am, Surat Al-Nahl, and others. Therefore, God Almighty said here, “That you may ride from them and eat from them. And for you therein are benefits and that you may attain thereby a need in your hearts, and upon them and upon ships you are carried.” And His Almighty saying, And He shows you His signs, meaning His proofs and evidence in the horizons and within yourselves. Then which of the signs of God will you deny? meaning that you are not able to deny any of His signs except by being stubborn and arrogant.

40:82: God Almighty tells us about the nations who denied the messengers in ancient times and what severe punishment befell them despite their great strength and the wealth they had accumulated on earth. But that did not avail them anything nor did it ward off from them an atom of God’s wrath. This is because when the messengers came to them with clear proofs, decisive arguments, and overwhelming evidence, they did not pay attention to them or accept them and were satisfied with what they had of knowledge, in their opinion, rather than what the messengers had brought them. Mujahid said: They said: We know more than them. We will not be resurrected and we will not be punished. Al-Suddi said: They rejoiced in what they had of knowledge despite their ignorance, so God Almighty’s wrath came to them that which they could not bear. And that which they used to ridicule encompassed them means it encompassed them. So when they saw Our wrath means they witnessed the punishment befalling them, “They said: We believe in God alone and we disbelieve in that which we used to associate with Him” meaning they believed in God Almighty and disbelieved in the tyrant, but where stumbling blocks are not said And no excuse will avail. This is like what Pharaoh said when he was about to drown: I believe that there is no god except that in whom the Children of Israel believe, and I am of the Muslims. God the Most High said: Now, although you disobeyed before and were among the corrupters.
